steps.say: Mixture of experts is a datacenter architecture, the post says. Looped transformers are a laptop architecture.
steps.caption: Huge weights, few active, against small weights reused

steps.say: This week two labs shipped a loop. So what does one actually cost?

scenes.headline: Looped transformers, priced in bytes
scenes.sub: Inkling 2 Mini and GLM-5.4 run the same layers more than once
scenes.say: I'm Mobius. A loop stores a block of layers once and runs it several times. You get depth without storing it.

steps.say: Inkling 2 Mini stores 24 layers. The first six and the last six run once.
The middle twelve are the core. Same weights every time.
The core runs three times, so one token passes through 48 layers from a file that holds 24.
steps.term: Effective depth: layers a token runs, not layers stored

steps.say: Each pass hands the next one a message, through a gate that starts closed. Early in training the loop does nothing.
Untie those passes and the same model needs 31.3 gigabytes at four bits. Looped, it is 16.6. Both read the same bytes per token.

scenes.credit: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini post, Figure 5

steps.say: The lab drew it the same way. The prelude feeds every pass.
Passes two and three also read the pass before.
steps.caption: The message, passed down

scenes.title: Read per token, batch 1
scenes.say: At batch 1, bytes read set the speed ceiling. The loop costs Mini 80 percent more reads. The experts are why it reads 4 gigabytes, not 16.

steps.say: Z.ai did not train from scratch. Looped models trained from scratch lag at the same compute, it says.
So it took its trained 750B base and looped 28 layers twice.
Gates keep the second pass from blowing up activations the rest of the model never saw.
And the second pass reuses the first pass's cache, so the extra loop costs one sliding window.
On a 30B twin with about 10 percent more training compute, the loop lifted AIME from 19.17 to 30.42.
And the answers got shorter. Some reasoning moved from text into depth.

scenes.credit: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini post, Figure 7

steps.say: Thinking Machines also released a model you can run at any loop count. On chained lookups with no chain of thought, every extra pass follows a longer chain.

scenes.label: DeepSWE, one pass against three, same checkpoint
scenes.say: One pass is a different model. DeepSWE goes from 0.7 percent to 47.4. Facts barely move: SimpleQA goes from 6.3 to 6.7.

scenes.quote: looping improves the model's reasoning, it doesn't enable its weights to store more facts

scenes.credit: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini post, Figure 8

steps.say: Does a loop hide its reasoning? At five passes the written reasoning was less than half as long, 1,661 tokens against 3,703, and just as legible.
It backtracked less. It did not hide steps, at this scale.
And the laptop? Mini is about 20 GB. The lab's demo ran it offline on a MacBook, on a flight.
steps.caption: Written and flown on the same laptop

scenes.text: A loop is a storage trick with a compute bill: depth you never store, paid in reads every token.
scenes.mark: storage trick with a compute bill

recap: A loop adds depth, not parameters
It costs reads and cache every pass
scenes.say: Depth, not parameters. Reads, every pass. Reasoning up, facts flat.
